items.statement: The determinant of the actual rotated cosine-grid precision is the product of its displayed diagonal values. \det A=\prod_{i=1}^{d}\lambda_i. \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix every actual \(O\in O(d)\), including either determinant sign. This assertion is pointwise; no Haar-law premise or determinant-one restriction is imposed. For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), define \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\), and the actual precision \(A=O\Lambda O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based \(j.\mathrm{val}+1/2\), corresponding to source \(i=j.\mathrm{val}+1\). The determinant is the genuine real finite determinant and the product ranges over every coordinate once. Orthogonality equations, determinant invariance and the diagonal-product identity are internal proved dependencies. No determinant, spectral-window, positivity or normalization identity is supplied as a new hypothesis. The source bounds are retained exactly, although the determinant algebra itself needs no interval restriction on the diagonal values. The actual Gaussian consumer uses these bounds to obtain positive definiteness from the existing source admissibility result. The real consumer is the same actual \(N(0,A^{-1})\) relative to Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Only its prefactor is independent of \(O\); the quadratic exponent retains the actual hidden orientation. The power \(d/2\) is real, including odd dimensions. The explicit-product density is a mathematical identity. The separate unweighted Gaussian integral/known-normalizer proposition, full C.4 calculus/minimizer, moments/Krylov, operational oracle/precision/TV/cost adapters and both complete main lower bounds remain open.
